changes: Author confidence lowered from medium to low: the cataloguer marks †samudāyakara† as corrupt, and it may not be a personal name at all (it could be read as 'samudāya-kṛtā', i.e. 'compiled').
Pakṣa normalised to śukla: 'te(!)' is most likely 'site' (bright fortnight). This fits the Durgotsava, whose saptamī falls in Āśvina śukla.
Year field: ŚS 1683 put in 'year', with VS 1818 recorded in as_written and notes.
Place normalized to Tanahun (Tanahũ), western Nepal.
Notes updated: both eras confirmed consistent (1683+78 = 1818-57 = 1761 CE).

date.as_written: āśvinaśya te(!) pakṣe saptamyāṃ ravivāsane || śrīśāke 1683 śri(!)saṃvat 1818

notes: The author's name is marked corrupt by the cataloguer (†samudāyakara†). It may be a garbled personal name, or not a name at all: 'samudāya-kṛtā' would mean 'compiled'. 'te(!) pakṣe' is probably 'site pakṣe' (bright fortnight), which fits Durgāpūjā saptamī in Āśvina śukla. The two eras agree: ŚS 1683 and VS 1818 both give 1761 CE (Sept/Oct 1761). No scribe or commissioner is named. 'tanahugrāmaśubhabham (!) astu' should be read as 'tanahugrāme, śubham astu'.
